status.statement: Engineering evidence prepared by a tool; not a subject review. An engineering agent cannot sign this packet.

taskIntent.purpose: Predict, then observe, how the slope of the tangent to f(x) = A·x² + B·x + C changes along the curve, how secant slopes compare with it as the second point moves closer, and how the derivative f′ records the slope at every x.

stages.instruction: Look at the graph of f(x) = A·x² + B·x + C and the probe point P. You can change the coefficients A, B and C to see different curves. Slopes, tangents and the derivative are not shown yet.
Before any slopes are shown, predict the slope of the curve at the probe point P.

response.prompt: Is the curve rising, falling or level at P, and roughly how steep is it there? How would the slope change if P moved to the right?

stages.instruction: Once the tangent at P and its slope f′(p) are shown, move P along the curve and compare the slope with your prediction. Then set the offset h to place a second point Q, and watch the secant slope as h gets closer to 0 from either side.
Once the graph of the derivative f′ is shown, move P and change the coefficients, and compare the height of the derivative graph at x = p with the slope of the tangent at P.
Explain in your own words how the slope of f changes along the curve and how the secant slope behaves as h shrinks.

response.prompt: How does the slope of the tangent at P change as P moves, how does the secant slope behave as h gets close to 0, and what does the derivative graph show?

stages.instruction: Explore freely: change the coefficients, move the probe and the second point, and compare the tangent, the secant and the derivative graph.

derivation.citation: Derivation written for this catalogue: expanding A·(x + h)² + B·(x + h) + C gives (f(x + h) − f(x))/h = 2A·x + B + A·h for every h ≠ 0, so the secant slope differs from f′(x) = 2A·x + B by exactly A·h and tends to it as h → 0; at h = 0 the quotient is 0/0. When A ≠ 0, f′(x) = 0 only at x = −B/(2A). Not independently reviewed.

Study Harness visualizer implementation report §12.1 and acceptance item A28: a bounded polynomial family with an analytically defined derivative, a movable probe, tangent, optional secant and linked slope values, a derivative plot shown only when authorized, and the linear, constant, zero-slope, coincident-secant, sign-change and domain-boundary cases.

assumptions: The function is exactly the quadratic f(x) = A·x² + B·x + C with real coefficients; A = 0 gives a straight line and A = B = 0 a constant.
The derivative is the analytical derivative f′(x) = 2A·x + B of this polynomial. It is not estimated from secant slopes, samples or a numerical limit.
Inputs are IEEE-754 double-precision values taken at their exact values; the second point is evaluated at the exact sum p + h.
Evaluation is deterministic on every conforming JavaScript engine: only exactly specified arithmetic is used, so the same parameters always give the same values.
limitations: Each quantity is its exact value rounded to the nearest double once. Categories come from exact signs, so a slope that displays as 0 can still be classified as increasing or decreasing.
A probe entered as a decimal is in general not exactly at a vertex whose position is not a binary fraction (for example −1/3), so the slope there is a small nonzero number.
The secant slope is undefined at h = 0 and no limiting value is substituted. For h ≠ 0 it differs from the derivative by exactly A·h.
The domain constraint −5 ≤ p + h ≤ 5 is evaluated on the double sum p + h, as by every runtime entry point; the exact sum can then lie outside by at most 2^−51, and Q is evaluated at that exact sum.

Values outside the double range are statuses: a nonzero value that rounds to zero is a numerical limit (UNDERFLOW), subnormal values carry a reduced-precision note, and the vertex of a curve with a tiny nonzero A can exceed the largest double (OVERFLOW).

The graphs of f and f′ are sampled at 401 positions from −5 to 5 in double precision; the polyline between samples does not certify values between them. Tangent and secant lines are drawn from correctly rounded endpoints, and an endpoint whose exact value is nonzero but below the double range is drawn at 0.

conventions.coordinate: x is horizontal and increases to the right; f(x) and f′(x) are vertical and increase upward. A slope is rise over run in these coordinates, so a positive slope rises to the right.

A.label: Coefficient A
A.description: Coefficient of x² in f(x) = A·x² + B·x + C. With A = 0 the function is linear or constant.

B.label: Coefficient B
B.description: Coefficient of x in f(x) = A·x² + B·x + C.

C.label: Coefficient C
C.description: Constant term of f(x) = A·x² + B·x + C; it shifts the graph up or down.

p.label: Probe position
p.description: x-coordinate of the probe point P = (p, f(p)) on the graph.

h.label: Secant offset
h.description: Horizontal offset from P to the second point Q, which lies at x = p + h. With h = 0 the two points coincide.

probe.x.label: Probe position
probe.x.meaning: x-coordinate of the probe point P; it repeats the parameter p exactly.
probe.x.signConvention: Positive to the right of x = 0.

probe.value.label: Function value at the probe
probe.value.meaning: f(p) = A·p² + B·p + C, the height of the graph at the probe, rounded once from its exact value.

derivative.label: Derivative at the probe
derivative.meaning: Analytical derivative f′(p) = 2A·p + B of the quadratic at the probe: the slope of the tangent at P, from the exact differentiation rule for this polynomial. It is not estimated from secant slopes, samples or a numerical limit.
derivative.signConvention: Positive when f increases as x increases (rise over run in the x–f(x) plane).

second.x.label: Second point position
second.x.meaning: x-coordinate p + h of the second point Q, rounded once from the exact sum (the same double the domain constraint checks). Equal to p when h = 0.
second.x.signConvention: Positive to the right of x = 0.

second.value.label: Function value at the second point
second.value.meaning: f(p + h) = A·(p + h)² + B·(p + h) + C for the exact sum p + h, rounded once.

secant.slope.label: Secant slope
secant.slope.meaning: Slope (f(p + h) − f(p))/h of the line through P and Q, which equals 2A·p + B + A·h exactly for h ≠ 0. Undefined (COINCIDENT_POINTS) when h = 0 because a secant needs two distinct points; it is never replaced by the derivative.
secant.slope.signConvention: Positive when f increases as x increases (rise over run in the x–f(x) plane).

secant.difference.label: Secant slope minus derivative
secant.difference.meaning: Difference between the secant slope and the analytical derivative at the probe, equal to A·h exactly for h ≠ 0; undefined (COINCIDENT_POINTS) when h = 0 because the secant slope is undefined.
secant.difference.signConvention: Positive when the secant is steeper upward (larger slope) than the tangent.

slope.sign.label: Direction of the graph at the probe
slope.sign.meaning: increasing when f′(p) > 0, decreasing when f′(p) < 0, stationary when f′(p) = 0; classified from the exact sign of 2A·p + B for the input values, never from rounded or displayed digits.
slope.sign.signConvention: Positive when f increases as x increases (rise over run in the x–f(x) plane).

curvature.label: Shape of the graph
curvature.meaning: positive-curvature when A > 0 (opens upward, slope increasing), negative-curvature when A < 0 (opens downward, slope decreasing), linear when A = 0 and B ≠ 0 (constant nonzero slope), constant when A = 0 and B = 0 (slope 0 everywhere).

vertex.x.label: Vertex position
vertex.x.meaning: x-coordinate −B/(2A) of the vertex, the only x where the analytical derivative is zero; one correctly rounded division. Undefined (NO_VERTEX) when A = 0 because a line has no vertex. It may lie outside the plotted domain.
vertex.x.signConvention: Positive to the right of x = 0.

constraints.message: The second point Q is at x = p + h, which must stay inside the plotted domain from −5 to 5.
constraints.recovery: Move the probe p or shorten the offset h so that p + h is between −5 and 5.

stages.instruction: Look at the graph of f(x) = A·x² + B·x + C and the probe point P. You can change the coefficients A, B and C to see different curves. Slopes, tangents and the derivative are not shown yet.
Before any slopes are shown, predict the slope of the curve at the probe point P.

response.prompt: Is the curve rising, falling or level at P, and roughly how steep is it there? How would the slope change if P moved to the right?

stages.instruction: Once the tangent at P and its slope f′(p) are shown, move P along the curve and compare the slope with your prediction. Then set the offset h to place a second point Q, and watch the secant slope as h gets closer to 0 from either side.
Once the graph of the derivative f′ is shown, move P and change the coefficients, and compare the height of the derivative graph at x = p with the slope of the tangent at P.
Explain in your own words how the slope of f changes along the curve and how the secant slope behaves as h shrinks.

response.prompt: How does the slope of the tangent at P change as P moves, how does the secant slope behave as h gets close to 0, and what does the derivative graph show?
